# Efir

> Free, open-source teleprompter with remote control for macOS, Windows, Linux and Android. Also called «Эфир» in Russian.

Native applications serve the shared web interface over a local HTTP/WebSocket server.
A phone joins by QR code over the same Wi-Fi. Local sessions do not need internet or WebRTC.
The hosted browser application uses PeerJS/WebRTC and needs internet for connection setup.
Android can read independently, host a session or join another host. Desktop applications open as controllers.

Features include fullscreen reading, horizontal/vertical mirroring, synchronized preview,
sections, speed controls, script storage, TXT/Markdown/DOCX import, portable backups and voice following.
UI languages: English, Russian, Spanish, Simplified Chinese, Hindi and Arabic.

Offline native speech depends on language support and installed models. Windows/Linux Vosk models are separate downloads.
Local HTTP phone browsers cannot access the microphone. Use native recognition on the host.
Current macOS binaries are ad hoc signed and not notarized by Apple. See the distribution guide for per-app opening instructions.
The local server has one shared session and does not store scripts. Scripts are stored on devices.
Efir's original source is MIT-licensed; dependencies retain their own licenses.
